SddScope.keywords: scope, discovery, vision, usage-example, design-variants, decision-log, scope-rules, living-spec, product, library, runtime-backing, sdd-scope-discovery
SddScope.Mission:
Author or evolve a `product` / `library` scope spec — a self-contained living spec: Vision, Usage Example, Requirements Gate, Architecture (Design Variants for product), Decision Log, Scope Rules, Bootstrap Requirements, Handoff to the `module` flow. Loaded lazily by the router; inherits the router core (language, dialogue, safeguard, diverge, no-narration, stateless) — not repeated here.
Input — scope name + intent (raw idea, or an existing spec for refine / pivot). Output — `specs//.spec.md`. scope-type is already `product` or `library` (the router sends `infrastructure` to the infra branch and `interface` to the interface branch).
Out of scope: module decomposition, entity inventory, DbC — those belong to the `module` flow. The project portal belongs to the root branch.
**Glossary.** Scope = architecturally cohesive unit (own runtime / stack / deployment / UX surface). Modes: greenfield (no spec) · refine (extend) · pivot (replace decisions, keep the trail) · rewrite (v0 clean-slate, no trail — `AX_PIVOT_REQUIRES_SUPERSESSION`).

BeliefState.deps: AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE, AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE, AX_DIALOGUE_DISCIPLINE, AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD, AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION, AX_STATELESS_ARTIFACT, AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH

SddScope.BeliefState:
Inherited from the loading directive (already in context): QUESTION_RULE_SLIM
Each directive runs in one of several modes, auto-detected from operator intake. Mode controls step branching and which axioms apply. The concrete mode set is directive-specific (e.g. `greenfield` / `refine` / `pivot`; `initial` / `extend-dag`; `initial` / `add-module` / `refine-module`).
Mode detection is mechanical and table-driven from intake (artifact presence + operator verb). Ambiguous intake never defaults silently → HALT and ask the operator (binary disambiguation where possible). The detection table is directive-specific.
A recommendation must be the result of a search, not the first typical answer. Aligned models collapse to the modal option; a single quick recommendation usually IS that mode, which is rarely the best fit for a specific task.
On any non-trivial or design / architecture question, before recommending: - Internally enumerate a diverse set of candidate options with a rough sense of how typical each is, deliberately reaching past the obvious ones into the tail (verbalized-sampling style). - Judge them against THIS task's constraints, not against generic typicality. - Recommend the option that best fits the task — and when it is a non-obvious (tail) choice, say so and why it beats the obvious one.
Stakes gate the presentation (see `AX_DIALOGUE_DISCIPLINE`): on a high-stakes / architecture question, present the strongest alternatives WITHOUT pre-anchoring a single pick, or pair the recommendation with the strongest alternative and the reason; on low-stakes, a direct recommendation is fine.
The `scope` flow reads `specs/README.md` for project context (vision, scope graph, sibling scopes). It MUST NOT rewrite the file. The narrow exception (per the `root` flow's `AX_PORTAL_PRIMARY_OWNER`): when the `scope` flow creates a brand-new scope, it MAY append one placeholder row to the Scopes table tagged `🚧 (awaiting root sync)`. Any other edit is forbidden — run the `root` flow instead.
The scope spec is a living document. In `refine` mode any section may be updated in place. There is no frozen 7 Handoff — the Handoff section evolves as modules are added.
`pivot` uses one-line Decision Log supersession: preserve the old entry; append a new `-DL-N` entry whose parenthetical carries the old→new delta, `supersedes: `, and the pre-rework git ref. The spec body is rewritten in place; git history is the full predecessor.
A V2 specification has one durable format. Greenfield authoring creates that format directly; refine/pivot edits it in place. Git diff shows changes for semantic judgment. Temporary Change Manifest, per-line review marks, Critic Rounds, publication state, and migration between V2 subformats are not part of the specification.
Before approval #1, run structural checks and one fresh independent semantic review of the complete target set. Resolve findings in the owning specs. Any semantic edit invalidates the old verdict, resets the human-readable approval marker to pending, and requires a fresh bounded review. The operator then approves the current artifacts and the specs record approval #1 per `ARTIFACT_APPROVAL_MARKER`. Implementation follows only after approval #1. Marker mechanics never use a content hash; the model judges staleness from the artifacts and Git evidence.
An editorial correction may use its exact mechanical verifier only when it changes no requirement, behavior, contract, inventory, architecture, dependency, BDD acceptance, risk, or Decision Log meaning. Any such delta is semantic and returns to the lifecycle above.
Phase reads specs only, never code; no project-wide search (grep / find / ripgrep) outside the reads explicitly listed by the directive. `audit` is the only directive permitted to read code; it alone resolves spec/code mismatch.
For product / library scopes the Approved Usage Example precedes Design Variants. DX shape: - For library: the public-API DX (init / happy path / error path with commentary). - For product app / spa / mobile / desktop: UX-flow DX. - For product cli-utility: CLI DX (commands, flags, exit codes, sample sessions). - For product service-module-sdk: API DX at the transport boundary.
DX is the consumer-driven baseline for downstream design; without it, Design Variants accumulate accidental complexity (over-engineering, speculative surface).
For product / library — this is the initial draft; ownership transfers post-first-`add-module` per `AX_SCOPE_SPEC_MODULE_MAP_OWNERSHIP` in module-decomposition.
The diagram floor for a scope spec is a fixed ladder, not one "when useful" picture — the same discipline agent-inbox's `AX_COMPREHENSION_LADDER` applies to a review applies here at design time instead of review time. Four rungs, each answering ONE distinct question, drawn in THIS order — requirements close BEFORE Use Cases and Data Flow are drawn, never the reverse, per the 2026-08-20 visualization-chain decision (`specs/ai-skills/research/2026-08-20-visualization-chain.research.md`): drawing the scenario picture only once the failure-mode requirements are locked means a failure branch on the diagram already traces to a real requirement ID, not a guess. 1. **Overview** — WHAT this scope is, system-context / high-level view. Unconditional. Held by tooling: `sdd-check` fails a missing section (`SDD_NO_DIAGRAM_BLOCK`) or an empty one (`SDD_DIAGRAM_BLOCK_EMPTY`). 2. **High-Level Architecture** — WHERE this scope sits AMONG its neighbours (C4-style boundary: this scope as a box, confirmed dependencies/consumers as boxes outside it) — distinct from Overview (Overview = the shape at a glance; this = the boundary, decided once Architecture is locked). Unconditional, drawn at `STEP_5_ARCHITECTURE` — see that step's Action for the concrete rule. 3. **Use Cases** — `product` scope-type only: actors → scenario, one line «зачем» each, the worst-case scenario marked distinctly (⚠️) — harvested from the «Потребители» / «Худший сценарий» topics closed during the `STEP_2_INTENT_CAPTURE` interview, but drawn only once `STEP_3_REQUIREMENTS_GATE` closes — see that step's Action for the concrete rule. 4. **Data Flow** — `product` AND `library`: a `flowchart` built from exactly four node kinds (external entity, process, store, labelled data-flow arrow) — NO conditions, NO loops, this is a data diagram, not a control-flow chart. Unconditional for both scope-types, drawn at `STEP_3_REQUIREMENTS_GATE` right after Use Cases — see that step's Action. All four are drawn as ASCII in chat at the step that owns them, BEFORE that step's Approval Check — a diagram appearing for the first time in the written spec means the operator never saw the shape they are approving (`AX_CHAT_BEFORE_SPEC`, `formats/diagram-vocabulary.xml`); an Approval Check without it is a show-before-ask violation the operator may reject and demand, the same class as the router's `H_ASK_WITHOUT_CARD`. Every diagram carries a caption naming the requirement IDs it shows, per `DIAGRAM_CAPTION_FORMAT` (`formats/diagram-vocabulary.xml`) — Overview and High-Level Architecture, being whole-scope pictures, may use the no-ID caption form the same contract allows. This ladder (rungs 1–4) is the mandatory floor for NEW scope specs only — a scope spec written before rungs 3–4 existed is not retroactively broken by their absence. Beyond this floor the author adds more views (sequence, before/after) wherever a further diagram genuinely helps a reader; that stays judgment, never a gate.
For product / library scope specs, runtime backing is declared at the scope level inside Requirements & Constraints under «Runtime Backing & Deferred Scope»: - Backing per major capability: `not-implemented` | `simulation` | `real-runtime`. - Deferred scope: parts whose real runtime is intentionally not delivered in v1, with reason. - Trust boundaries that require a real runtime hook (auth, payments, persistence) are listed explicitly.
Declaring backing early prevents `module-decomposition` and `task-scaffolding` from misclassifying simulation seams as real implementations.
For scope-type=product and scope-type=library:
**Requirements gate before design.** Architecture variants are forbidden until REQUIREMENTS_GATE is closed. Required: Functional Requirements, Non-Functional Constraints, Out-of-Scope, Project-Wide Rules (Rules).
**Usage Example gate.** An Approved Usage Example is mandatory before Design Variants. library → Public API DX. product → UX-flow DX or CLI DX depending on Project Type.
**Project Type scales depth** (product only): - `app` (mobile / desktop / spa): 2–3 architectural variants. - `service-module-sdk`: 2–3 variants across transport + persistence. - `cli-utility`: 1–2 variants (minimal depth).
**YAGNI guard.** Only abstractions needed for v1. Future-proof extensions without a confirmed consumer are forbidden.
The directive runs on an explicit frame stack with a defined main path of phases. Disputes / dives / sub-topics open a nested frame; the stack is visible in the trace header. A sub-topic never silently stalls the parent frame. The concrete main path is directive-specific.
Every non-obvious decision → a Decision Log entry in `DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT` — one line, the expanded part in parentheses: `-DL-N — (почему: …; отвергнуто: …; риск: …)`; IDs are stable. Non-obvious only (`AX_DECISION_LOG_NON_OBVIOUS`): a pick already recorded in the spec's own tables is never duplicated as a DL row. Which decisions qualify and which Decision Log receives the entry are specified per directive.
In `pivot` mode, preserve the prior entry byte-for-byte and append one new one-line `-DL-N — (...)` entry; its parenthetical names the old→new delta, `supersedes: `, and the git ref for the pre-rework state. The prior id may be a legacy `D-N` only when it already existed; never rewrite append-only history just to rename it. Pivot Invalidation List enumerates downstream artifacts requiring `refine-module` / reopen — consumed by `audit` via `AX_STALE_AFTER_PIVOT_VERIFICATION`.
`rewrite` mode is the exception: a pre-production / v0 scope with no production backing, whose old content was scratch that helps nothing going forward. It replaces the spec from a clean slate — NO supersession trail, NO Pivot Invalidation List (nothing downstream to keep coherent; git history is the only record). Use `pivot` (keep the trail) whenever the scope has any production backing or downstream consumers; use `rewrite` only for genuine v0 throwaway. Enforcement: a scope that already has downstream artifacts on disk (module specs or task tickets) is by definition NOT v0 — `rewrite` is forbidden there; halt and use `pivot`.
Scope-wide rules are declared in spec Rules. Categories with directory mapping: - coding → `ai/directives/coding/.xml` - testing → `ai/directives/testing/.xml` - architecture → `ai/directives/architecture/.xml` - infra → `ai/directives/infra/.xml`
Every rule reference must resolve to an existing file. Missing → operator picks resolution IN-SESSION (never a halt, never an autonomous task): - **skip** — tool's own defaults are the discipline; record in Decision Log. - **research-and-author** — agent WebFetches authoritative docs (official source from `package.json#homepage` or operator-supplied URL), drafts rule file, operator approves before write to `ai/directives//.xml`. Drafts capture TIMELESS engineering practice only — discipline, trade-offs, anti-pattern categories, binary invariants. NOT captured: version numbers, CLI flags, config-syntax snippets, plugin lists (those churn between releases; they live in `package.json` / config files). - **defer** — record as Open Risk in Handoff with `Owner: operator-action`; proceed.
Operator refuses to choose → `H_MISSING_RULE_FILE`. Otherwise no halt.
**Every rule activates through an explicit operator decision — never silently.** The decision is two-staged: Stage A locks the relevance shortlist per category with the operator; Stage B walks the axioms of `architecture/*` and `infra/*` rules for Accept (default) / Adapt / Override. Every deviation from a rule default lands in the Decision Log. `coding/*` / `testing/*` rules stay deferred — the phase-subagent loads them at phase entry per `phase-execution-protocol`.
Scope spec declares `depends-on` edges in Scope Dependencies. These edges feed cascade computation in the `scaffold` flow. Cross-scope contracts are sourced from `interface`-type scopes — never described inside a product scope spec.
Introducing a parallel mechanism where an existing one from a neighbour spec could be extended is a decision at GOAL level, never a silent author call. "Вводим новое" is a valid answer ONLY when it names the specific neighbour invariant / requirement ID the existing mechanism cannot satisfy, and records the choice as its own Decision Log entry (`DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT`) citing that ID. No cited ID, no entry → the mechanism stays unjustified: route it back to the operator as an open question, not a decision already made on their behalf. This governs the AUTHOR's system-fit check (`STEP_*_SYSTEM_FIT` in `scope` / `module` / `interface` / `infra`); `AX_REUSE_FIRST` runs the same bias against duplication from the CRITIC's reactive vantage, after the artifact already exists — the two apply one belief at two different points in the lifecycle, not two competing rules.
Separate Facts / Assumptions / Hypotheses in every intake-style frame. - **Facts** — directly observable from input artifacts (spec, sibling specs, rule files, extracted measurements). - **Assumptions** — working assumptions awaiting confirmation; mark explicitly. - **Hypotheses** — conjectures that require operator validation before they are promoted to requirements.
Conflating the three causes downstream decisions to be made on unvalidated assumptions, producing requirements mismatches that surface only at integration; surface them in distinct lists.
External research (WebSearch/WebFetch) run in this session ALWAYS lands as a research document via `npx gennady sdd-new research --scope --slug ` — filled in BEFORE the result feeds a proposal to the operator; a chat summary is not storage (session dies, research dies with it). Every factual claim must be re-verifiable: traced to a source (a specific page, URL + access date; for code-derived facts — path + commit) OR explicitly flagged `agent conclusion` / `from model memory as of `. A fact carrying neither is a document defect, not a style choice. A repeat question checks existing `specs/**/research/` first — supersede, never duplicate.
Prefer primary evidence: official documentation, repository/release notes, standards, or papers. A secondary comparison may supplement but never solely support a tool/version/API decision. The candidate analysis remains immutable after it is shown. Once the operator decides, update only `FINAL_DISPOSITION`: outcome, the actual spec/Decision Log choice, and its delta from the research recommendation. A later critic change updates the same disposition or marks the document superseded.
Discovery is design-blind to repository code (per `AX_SPEC_IS_SOLE_SOURCE`) **except** inside the External Dependencies Audit step, where narrow Read is permitted **only for inventory verification** — confirming whether a referenced package, file, scope, or tool physically exists. Permitted reads there: `package.json` and equivalents, `tsconfig.json` and equivalents, `specs/README.md`, sibling scope manifests, filesystem existence checks. Forbidden there: reading application source code to influence design decisions — inventory verification answers "does X exist", never "how does X work internally". An existing mechanism this audit turns up — one the spec should extend instead of duplicating — MUST feed back into the design: revising Architecture / Contracts on that finding is the ordinary continuation of THIS session's drafting, not a separate ceremony, as long as the spec has not yet merged to master (`AX_PIVOT_REQUIRES_SUPERSESSION` governs a revision raised after that point). Pop back to the relevant earlier step explicitly, incorporate the finding, then re-run the External Dependencies Audit once more before writing the final spec.
A scope spec has a bounded role: Vision, Requirements, Architecture decisions, Decision Log, Module Map, composition Usage Example, Handoff, Bootstrap Requirements. Entity inventory, public surfaces, DbC contracts, and file layout are module-level — they live ONLY in module specs (`AX_HIERARCHICAL_SPECS`), never inline in the scope spec.
Two representations: - **monolithic** — no modules yet; the scope spec may hold design inline (early / small scope). - **index** — once decomposed, the scope spec is a thin composition over its modules: Module Map + Usage Example linking to each module's usage example; the detail lives in the modules.
Growth is the decomposition signal, not a license to expand. When scope-level design reaches entity / contract / file granularity, that detail moves into a module — it does NOT accumulate in the scope spec. A scope converges to a thin index; it does not grow without bound.
First decomposition is an authoring refactor: the `initial` module invocation moves entity-level detail out of the scope spec into new module specs, leaving the scope spec in the index representation. The same rule recurses — a module that reaches sub-module granularity sheds detail into sub-modules and stays an index over them.
Held by tooling: `sdd-check` flags a bloated scope index (`SDD_SCOPE_BLOATED`) and, recursing the same rule to a module with child modules beneath it, a parent module that has not become a thin index (`SDD_PARENT_MODULE_NOT_INDEX`).
Module decomposition accepts a structurally complete `product` or `library` scope draft as the next authoring step before approval #1. It creates/updates the module specs needed to make the complete spec set reviewable. For an already-approved scope, add/refine module work is also valid. Neither case depends on a session working set, temporary manifest, or bare approval label. Infrastructure remains the sole no-module scope type.
The resulting complete scope+module spec set runs one independent semantic review and operator approval #1 before scaffold. A later semantic change repeats that boundary.
Before writing any operator-facing artifact, recall the language rules — `AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE` (bureaucratic noun-for-verb phrasing, literal calque, bookish word) and `AX_READER_WITHOUT_SESSION_CONTEXT` (a branch name, «как обсуждали», a session-plan label) — and hold the text about to be written to them. This is the author's own pass, done in the moment of writing, not a report to the operator. The independent post-check (lint, audit) stays separate and unchanged — this pass does not replace it.
A mutation is not done until its scope passes the mechanical check. Any flow that creates or evolves an artifact under a scope — spec, module, ticket, DAG, tracker — closes by running `sdd-check` on the affected scope (`sdd-check --all specs/`; portal, task-DAG, tracker, or cross-scope work → `sdd-check --all .`) and resolving or consciously deferring every finding before handing off.
SddScope.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_NO_INTAKE` | Empty intake | | `H_AMBIGUOUS_MODE` | Spec exists + mode verb absent (per `AX_MODE_AUTO_DETECT_OR_HALT`) | | `H_AMBIGUOUS_PRODUCT_LIBRARY` | Operator intent leaves product vs library unclear after STEP_1_CONFIRM | | `H_LOW_CONFIDENCE` | Confidence `LOW` while locking architecture | | `H_REQ_NOT_APPROVED` | Design Variants attempted without a closed Requirements Gate | | `H_GOLDEN_NOT_APPROVED` | Design Variants attempted without an approved Usage Example | | `H_SYSTEM_FIT_NOT_RUN` | `STEP_5_ARCHITECTURE` entered before `STEP_4B_SYSTEM_FIT`'s checklist closed, or "вводим новое" recorded without the specific neighbour invariant/requirement ID it fails (`AX_PARALLEL_MECHANISM_REQUIRES_JUSTIFICATION`) | | `H_MISSING_RULE_FILE` | A rule reference does not resolve to an existing file | | `H_PIVOT_NO_INVALIDATION_LIST` | `pivot` mode without a Pivot Invalidation List | | `H_REWRITE_WITH_DOWNSTREAM` | `rewrite` mode but the scope already has module specs / tickets — not v0, use `pivot` (`AX_PIVOT_REQUIRES_SUPERSESSION`) | | `H_BOOTSTRAP_REQUIREMENTS_MISSING` | STEP_8 finished without a Bootstrap Requirements section | | `H_OPERATOR_REJECT` | Operator rejected the spec |

Step.Goal: Resolve scope name and mode; gather context.
Step.Action: State from the router already gives the portal + scope-type (product / library). Resolve the scope name from intake (or ask). Stat `specs//.spec.md`: absent → `greenfield`; present → detect the mode per `AX_DIRECTIVE_MODE` / `AX_MODE_AUTO_DETECT_OR_HALT`. Read the rule registry for available rules (per `AX_SCOPE_RULES_DECLARATION`).

Step.Goal: Confirm product vs library and outline the section set.
Step.Action: Carry the router's scope-type and mode forward. Ask only if product vs library remains genuinely ambiguous; otherwise outline the sections inline with STEP_2 and spend no dedicated Ask.

Step.Goal: Lock the scope's goal and primary constraints.
Step.Action:
Intent Candidate (1–3 bullets). Evidence Hygiene per `AX_EVIDENCE_HYGIENE` (Facts / Assumptions / Hypotheses, separated). Then run the operator interview — `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/interview-protocol.directive.xml")` — passing the scope-type (product / library — selects the TopicCatalog block) and the confirmed `scale:` from the session file: per `AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH` the map depth follows scale — `fix` / `function` → base topics + the triage minimum; `product` → the full scope-type block. The interview IS the substance of the step. A dispute or side-topic raised mid-interview opens a nested frame on the flow's stack — this step's main path never silently stalls on it (`AX_STACK_BASED_FLOW`). Capture the initial Runtime Backing posture per `AX_RUNTIME_BACKING_EXPLICIT`.
For `product` scope-type, this step closes the «Потребители» and «Худший сценарий» topics — the raw material for the Use Cases diagram. Per the 2026-08-20 visualization-chain decision (requirements close BEFORE use cases are drawn, never the reverse), this step does NOT draw that diagram — the drawing happens at `STEP_3_REQUIREMENTS_GATE`, once the Requirements Gate closes (rung 3 of `AX_SPEC_MANDATORY_DIAGRAM`); see that step's Action. Approval Check. STOP.

Functional · Non-Functional · Out-of-Scope. For product: + Runtime Backing (per `AX_RUNTIME_BACKING_EXPLICIT`) + Project-Wide Rules (per `AX_SCOPE_RULES_DECLARATION`). Close the remaining holes via `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/interview-protocol.directive.xml")` — focus: only the topics the Requirements Gate still misses; map depth sized to the session-file `scale:` per `AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH`.
Once the requirements list is drafted — including the нештатная entries, a failure branch without a locked requirement ID has nothing to caption — draw the two diagrams the 2026-08-20 visualization-chain decision moves to this point, per `AX_SPEC_MANDATORY_DIAGRAM`: 1. `product` scope-type ONLY — the Use Cases diagram (rung 3): actors → scenario nodes, one line «зачем» each, harvested from the «Потребители» / «Худший сценарий» topics closed at `STEP_2_INTENT_CAPTURE`, the worst-case scenario marked distinctly (⚠️) — as its own ASCII block in chat; a bare bullet list of user types does not satisfy this rung. 2. `product` AND `library` — the Data Flow diagram (rung 4, `DFD` type per `formats/diagram-vocabulary.xml`): a `flowchart` built from exactly four node kinds — external entity, process, store, labelled data-flow arrow — NO conditions, NO loops (a data diagram, not a control-flow chart); ≤7 nodes; as its own ASCII block in chat. Each diagram's caption names the requirement IDs it shows, per `DIAGRAM_CAPTION_FORMAT` (`formats/diagram-vocabulary.xml`) — `_<что показывает> — -REQ-[, -REQ-]._`. **Both diagrams shown (Data Flow always; Use Cases when scope-type=product), this message, before the Approval Check below** — their absence is a show-before-ask violation, the same class as the router's `H_ASK_WITHOUT_CARD`; the operator may reject and demand them. Record the closed set for STEP_5's consolidated design packet; ask here only if a blocking requirement fork remains (`H_REQ_NOT_APPROVED`).

Step.Goal: Lock the Approved Usage Example (mandatory before architecture).
Step.Action: Per `AX_DX_FIRST`, write a real-code usage example: library → Public API DX; product → UX-flow or CLI DX (depth per Project Type). Carry it into STEP_5's consolidated design packet; ask here only if a new fork remains (else `H_GOLDEN_NOT_APPROVED`).

Step.Goal: Reconcile with the existing system before architecture locks.
Step.Action:
FIRST action this step: run orientation ToolCall below (this works even before `sdd-new` materializes the spec — a greenfield scope-type is not a reason to skip the call). Read its output in full: the portal line, the one-hop neighbours with their paths, entity/contract NAMES, requirement IDs + titles, the consumers list, and its closing question — the tool's bounded extract is the evidence, not a repo scan (`AX_BOOTSTRAP_NARROW_READ` governs the LATER code-level narrow read at STEP_8; this read is spec-level, via the tool, and comes first).
Then close, in THIS message, the fixed checklist — record every answer in the spec (Decision Log entry when (a)/(b) lands on "new", inline note otherwise): (a) Is this entity/mechanism already an existing kind — does the extract already name it? (b) If not: which existing mechanism the extract names are we EXTENDING instead of introducing a new one? (c) Which neighbour specs (paths, from the extract) will need work for this to fit the system — each is recorded in the owning dependency/impact section or Pivot Invalidation List? (d) Which neighbour requirements (IDs, from the extract) conflict with what we are about to lock, and how is the conflict resolved? "Вводим новое" answers (a)/(b) ONLY together with the specific neighbour invariant/requirement ID the existing mechanism cannot satisfy, plus its own Decision Log entry (`AX_PARALLEL_MECHANISM_REQUIRES_JUSTIFICATION`) — "проще с нуля" is not a citation, else `H_SYSTEM_FIT_NOT_RUN`. On a genuinely greenfield project with no neighbours, `sdd-orient` degenerates to its one-line "соседей нет" — the checklist still runs, (a) still gets an honest answer, (c)/(d) collapse to "н/д"; the step itself is never skipped. These answers feed STEP_5's consolidated design packet; they are not a dedicated confirmation surface. npx gennady sdd-orient --scope Inputs : =operator-confirmed scope retained by this flow. Use orientation.

Research gate before drafting: at scale `product` / `library` — mandatory, 2–3 targeted WebSearch queries on how market leaders solve THIS scope's requirements and how they architect for them; at scale `module` / `function` — proportional per `AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH` (light pass, or skip with a one-line rationale); at scale `fix` — skipped, no research. Where it runs, persist it per `AX_RESEARCH_PERSISTED` before the Design Variants / Architecture below are drafted with researchManifest ToolCall below, filled (STATUS/PROBLEM/CRITERIA/OPTIONS/DECISION/CONSEQUENCES/EVIDENCE/RELATED) — and link the document in this message and in the Decision Log entry's RELATED (parentheses) once the variant is picked at STEP_6. Inputs , : this STEP_5 research context. npx gennady sdd-new research --scope --slug Use researchManifest.
library → Architecture: public surface structure, key patterns, briefly-rejected alternatives. product → Design Variants per `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` — reach past the obvious option into the tail; judge each against THIS scope, do not collapse to the modal design. Variant count follows the session-file `scale:` per `AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH` (Project Type refines it per `AX_PRODUCT_LIBRARY_FLOW`): scale `product` → 2–3 variants; scale `module` / `function` → 1–2, or a single design with the skip rationale recorded in the Decision Log. Under `LOW` confidence do not lock (`H_LOW_CONFIDENCE`).
Before the Approval Check, draw the scope-boundary diagram (rung 2 of `AX_SPEC_MANDATORY_DIAGRAM`, C4-style, per `formats/diagram-vocabulary.xml`): THIS scope as a boundary box, its known neighbours as boxes outside it — depends-on (infra-base / other scopes, from the Portal Scope Graph already in state) and provides-to (consumer scopes), plus whatever Scope Dependencies are confirmed so far — ≤7 nodes, as an ASCII block in THIS message. This IS the Overview system-context shape decided now, for THIS scope's place among neighbours; `STEP_9_FINAL_SPEC` converts the same drawing to mermaid inside both `## Overview` and `## High-Level Architecture` (`AX_CHAT_BEFORE_SPEC`) — never invented fresh at write time. **Diagram shown, this message, before the Approval Check below** — its absence is a show-before-ask violation, the same class as the router's `H_ASK_WITHOUT_CARD`; the operator may reject and demand it. Present requirements, Usage Example, architecture, system-fit consequences, and non-default rule deltas as ONE consolidated design packet. Approval Check. STOP.
library → skip to STEP_7. product → operator picks a variant; record a Decision Log entry per `AX_DECISION_LOG_REQUIRED` (`DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT`). STOP.

Step.Goal: Lock the active rule set for this scope.
Step.Action: Run the rule activation per `AX_RULE_ACTIVATION` against the registry read at STEP_0: 1. Stage A — per category, shortlist «recommend activate» + «considered, recommend skip», each with a one-line rationale scoped to THIS scope. Operator agrees / expands / contracts → list locked; deviations → Decision Log entry (`DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT`). 2. Stage B — for `architecture/*` and `infra/*` rules on the locked list: read only `Mission`, `Belief_State`, `Reward_Criteria` of the rule file; surface each axiom with a rationale → operator Accept (default) / Adapt / Override — Adapt and Override each land in the Decision Log. Keep it light on uncontroversial axioms. `coding/*` / `testing/*` stay deferred to phase entry. Record the locked list in Project-Wide Rules per `AX_SCOPE_RULES_DECLARATION`; a reference that resolves to no file → `H_MISSING_RULE_FILE`. Defaults implied by the selected stack require no Ask; only Adapt/Override deltas reopen the consolidated design decision.

Step.Goal: Reconcile the drafted spec with repository reality; materialize Bootstrap Requirements.
Step.Action: Walk the drafted spec; extract every external assumption (packages, workspace links, tools, pre-existing files, cross-scope types, env / services, structural prerequisites). Classify each `exists` | `missing` | `unknown` — narrow read for inventory only, per `AX_BOOTSTRAP_NARROW_READ` and `AX_SPEC_IS_SOLE_SOURCE` (no reading app source for design). Resolve every `missing` / `unknown` with the operator (source · version · owner), each a Decision Log entry. Record every confirmed cross-scope assumption as a `depends-on` edge in Scope Dependencies per `AX_CROSS_SCOPE_DEPENDENCIES` (cross-scope contracts come from `interface` scopes). Materialize the canonical six-column Bootstrap Requirements table. Every task-owned `package` row names exact `package.json, package-lock.json` Gate Artifacts. Node/npm runtime artifacts (`.nvmrc`, the Node fields in `package.json`, `.npmrc`) belong to the same or an upstream scope before any dependency install. Readiness rows additionally name exact `Readiness Gates` and repo-relative `Gate Artifacts`; non-readiness rows use `—`. Gate: empty list only if explicitly «nothing to bootstrap», else `H_BOOTSTRAP_REQUIREMENTS_MISSING`. An existing mechanism this audit turns up feeds back into Architecture / Contracts now, in the same authoring pass — per `AX_BOOTSTRAP_NARROW_READ`, pop back to the relevant earlier step, incorporate it, re-run this audit once more; only a finding raised after the spec has already merged to master needs a formal `pivot`.

In `greenfield`/`rewrite` mode, when `specs//.spec.md` does not exist yet, create its skeleton via productManifest ToolCall below (or libraryManifest ToolCall below) — the command never overwrites and prints the section manifest (which sections are REQUIRED and what to fill); in `refine`/`pivot` mode the file already exists, edit it in place, skip `sdd-new`. Content guidance per `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE` the matching format — `ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/product-spec-structure.xml` (product) or `ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/library-spec-structure.xml` (library); Bootstrap Requirements is part of every spec. Keep the spec inside its bounded role per `AX_SCOPE_STAYS_THIN` — entity / contract / file-level detail belongs to module specs. Before writing, run the self-check pass per `AX_ARTIFACT_STYLE_SELF_CHECK`. In `refine` mode update sections in place per `AX_LIVING_SPEC`. In `pivot` mode also `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/pivot-formats.xml")` (Pivot Invalidation List + rework entries) per `AX_PIVOT_REQUIRES_SUPERSESSION`; in `rewrite` mode write fresh — no supersession, no invalidation list. For a brand-new scope, append the `🚧 (awaiting root sync)` placeholder row to the portal Scopes table per `AX_PORTAL_READ_ONLY_WITH_PLACEHOLDER_EXCEPTION` — every other portal edit belongs to the root flow. Write the ordinary V2 spec directly per `AX_SPEC_LIFECYCLE`; Git diff carries the review delta and no temporary manifest or line marks are added. Record affected neighbour paths and requirement conflicts in their owning Architecture/Dependencies/Decision Log fields. `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/preflight-protocol.directive.xml")` and run its lazy active-domain checklist. Then close with the integrity check per `AX_CLOSE_WITH_INTEGRITY_CHECK`: run integrityCheck ToolCall below (anchor balance + required sections + links) and resolve any finding. Then Branch by decomposition and impact — missing/ambiguous evidence fails closed: - New / rewritten `product` or `library`, or `refine` / `pivot` with incomplete decomposition: hand the structurally complete scope draft directly to module decomposition per `AX_HANDOFF_TO_MODULE_DECOMPOSITION`. The module owner creates/resolves module specs, then the complete set receives one review and approval #1. Completeness is structural: the non-empty Module Map must resolve one-to-one to every canonical module spec on disk. - `refine` / `pivot` changes a module boundary or contract: first use the `module` flow to update every affected module in ordinary V2 format. Then review one target-set = changed scope + ALL module specs; unchanged modules are read-only members. - `refine` / `pivot` is scope-only and leaves all module boundaries/contracts unchanged, with decomposition already complete: keep existing modules as read-only reviewer context. Do not edit them. Review one target-set whose changed member is the scope, while the review-set still names every module spec. A standalone `infrastructure` scope is the sole no-module exception, but its actually changed scope artifact still runs the same review lifecycle. Load `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/review-lifecycle.directive.xml")` once for the selected target-set. Only the independently reviewed product/library bundle (or reviewed infrastructure exception) may be approved. After a scope-only refine/pivot returns from semantic review and approval #1, determine its downstream outcome once: no task/DAG impact → finish as a spec-only change and enter the terminal handling below; task/DAG impact → load scaffold and extend the existing DAG. New/incomplete decomposition hands off to module authoring. Every owner reconstructs context from actual artifacts. If chained work remains, offer continue or «Пауза — продолжу позже»; pause prints the exact next skill/scope. When no work remains, report completion. The approval question is a normal stop, not a persistent terminal state. npx gennady sdd-new product --scope Use productManifest. npx gennady sdd-new library --scope Use libraryManifest. npx gennady sdd-check --all specs/ Use integrityCheck.

SddScope.ChatOutput:
Service line — dim, internal, never narrated (per `AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION`): `🦾 DSC_R · · · · conf=`. Breadcrumb milestones (per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`): Intent · Requirements · Usage Example · Architecture · Rules · Spec. Disputes / dives open a nested frame on the main path per `AX_STACK_BASED_FLOW`; render the dive per `SIDE_DIVE_FORMAT` and return to the parent frame.
A step-boundary / decision message (the decision card) is sectioned with markdown headers, in this order. Skip any section empty for this step. During free dialogue inside a step the agent does NOT print this layout — it just talks.
`` — internal anchor + scope + mode + confidence (supplied by the branch)
`` — per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`, its OWN paragraph (a blank line above it, not just a `\n`) — markdown collapses a single newline into a space, so without the blank line the breadcrumb visually fuses onto the service line
## `` `` — одной фразой, что делаем
### 🤔 Как я понял задачу — an italic blockquote (`> _…_`), 2–3 sentences max: the task retold in the agent's own words plus the single riskiest assumption, linked by wording to the question that resolves it; never a restate of already-settled content — only what is NEW or could be misread (goes at the TOP) ### 🎯 Главное решение — the crux in plain words; if the decision is a flow (data moving, state transitions, start/stop conditions), add a small ASCII diagram — the one place a fenced block is allowed in this message, at most one per message ### 💡 <О чём решаем> — per `QUESTION_RULE_SLIM` (full format with worked examples lives in `QUESTION_FORMAT`, in the interview / vision directives) ### ↓ Детали — по желанию — reasoning, full comparison, change-list (per `AX_PROGRESSIVE_DISCLOSURE`)
Glyph dictionary — closed inventory, one assigned meaning each, never a free pick. Every glyph here is chosen to read clearly on BOTH a light and a dark terminal/chat theme — half-tone shading characters (`░ ▒ ▓` and similar) are forbidden anywhere in this layout: they render as near-invisible or vanish outright depending on theme.
Section-header glyphs (fixed, one per header, in the order above): - `🤔` — the agent's own understanding check, at the top of a decision card - `🎯` — the crux decision, in plain words - `💡` — a decision the agent is proposing for the operator to confirm or pick between - `↓` — folded detail, expand on demand
Step-TYPE glyphs (fixed, keyed by the step's TYPE, used in the service line / breadcrumb, never a free pick): - `🏗` — creation / scaffold (new spec, new tickets, new files) - `🔍` — audit / review (fresh-eyes read, no write) - `🔧` — fix / reconcile (spec ⟷ code drift repair) - `⚡` — execute (a task ticket's phases running) - `🗺` — routing / overview (intent classification, project-level map)
Breadcrumb-status glyphs (per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`): `✅` done · `👷` active · `◻️` not yet.
No other emoji appear in message or section headers — the glyphs enumerated above are the only ones this layout permits.
One line, its own paragraph below the service line — a blank line separates the two (per `MESSAGE_LAYOUT`); a single `\n` with no blank line is a contract defect, markdown renders it fused onto the service line as one run-on. This session's milestones, each rendered ` `, with a status marker chosen for legibility on BOTH light and dark themes — no half-tone shading characters (`░ ▒ ▓`) anywhere, they vanish depending on theme. Status set: `✅` done · `👷` active (the step running now) · `◻️` not yet reached. Delta only; never re-list everything already settled. This is the «where are we», and it replaces a verbose run-on of finished steps.
`Vision ✅ · Scope Graph 👷 · Infra ◻️ · Portal ◻️`
A sub-topic dive inside a step collapses to two lines, not a five-field Return Summary:
→ ушли в `<тема>` ← `<итог одной фразой>`
Decision first, reasoning on demand. The must-read top of a message is short: where we are + my read + what to decide. Everything heavy — full option comparison, evidence, the change-list, derivations — goes BELOW a `### ↓ Детали — по желанию` header. Never dump reasoning above the questions. Facts already verified collapse to one line («сверился: …»); uncertainties that need the operator BECOME the questions — never list them twice.

ArtifactOutput.Contract:
One line per entry — no Status/Recorded fields, no multi-line block. The parenthetical carries only what applies; omit a clause entirely rather than writing it empty.
```markdown -DL-N — (почему: ; отвергнуто: ; риск: ) ```
**ID.** `-DL-` — spec acronym first, exactly like a Task-ID and like `-REQ-` (`REQUIREMENT_ENTRY_FORMAT`); `` is sequential within THIS spec only — the acronym gives global uniqueness, not the number. This is the only grammar for NEW entries. Existing append-only file-local `D-N` entries remain immutable and resolvable as legacy references; never create another; conflicts (a duplicate number inside one spec) are caught mechanically, the same way as for `-REQ-`.
Superseding a prior decision appends `; supersedes: -DL-M` to the parenthetical instead of a separate field — the entry stays one line. `` is the recording date (`YYYY-MM-DD`); status (active / superseded / rejected / deferred) is implicit from prose and from whether a later entry supersedes this one — a spec has no dangling "rejected" or "deferred" entries sitting as if active, the prose says so directly (e.g. `отвергнуто в пользу X` folded into the same line that would have recorded it, never a standalone rejected entry with its own `-DL-N`).
